Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Salt Lake City UT
244 PM MDT Mon Oct 12 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...


- A Pacific Northwest low will be the dominant weather feature
  over the region through the middle of the week. Pairing with an
  abundant amount of moisture from tropical cyclone remnants,
  widespread precipitation with an elevated potential for flash
  flooding along with cooler temperatures and lowering snow
  levels, bringing accumulating mountain snow is expected through
  at least Tuesday.

- Some outlying valleys, including the Cache Valley, may see
  freezing temperatures as early as Tuesday morning, with freezing
  temperatures becoming more widespread Wednesday and Thursday
  mornings. 

- Conditions will steadily dry for the latter half of the week
  with a gradual warming trend in temperatures through the
  weekend.  

&&

.DISCUSSION...A slow moving Pacific storm system will begin to
progress through the region over the next 48 hours, bringing
continued rainfall and even some high elevation snowfall. Moisture
&&

.AVIATION...

KSLC...MVFR conditions with pockets of VFR will persist for the KSLC 
&&

.FIRE WEATHER, Issued 149 AM MDT Mon Oct 12 2026...
A slow moving low pressure system combined with ample
moisture across the region will continue to bring widespread wetting 
rains through Tuesday. As this low slowly makes its way through the
region, cooler air will lower snow levels into the 7000 to 8000 
foot range tonight through Tuesday. With widespread precipitation 
along with cooler air spreading into the region, temperatures will
remain well below normal through midweek along with high relative
humidity. Precipitation may linger into the day Wednesday as this
low pressure system begins to exit the region. High pressure will 
bring a warming and drying trend for the latter portion of the week. 

&&

.SLC WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
UT...Flood Watch until 6 PM MDT this evening for UTZ101>131.

&&
